text:
### Observed differences

- A block of six activities — A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26, entered after A31 and followed by A32 — occurs together in essentially every trace in both windows, but its internal order changed. In the earlier window several orders coexisted: A20 came before A26 in about 49 in 100 traces and A26 before A20 in about 50 in 100, A24 came before A20 in about 73 in 100, and A26 came before A23 in about 70 in 100. In the later window every one of these pairs runs in a single direction (A20 before A26 in about 98 in 100, A20 before A24 in about 99 in 100, A23 before A24 in about 97 in 100). [REL014, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL021]
- Successor profiles match: earlier, A31 split its exits about equally between A24 and A22, A23 most often led to A32 (about 48 in 100) but also frequently to A26, A25 or A24, and A24 often led back to A20, A22 or A23. In the later window each activity has one dominant successor: A31→A22 (99 in 100), A22→A20 (98), A20→A23 (99), A23→A24 (98), A24→A26 (99), A26→A25 (99), A25→A32 (90). [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013]
- Positional distances now follow one chain, A31→A22→A20→A23→A24→A26→A25→A32: A31 reaches A20 exactly two positions later in about 99 in 100 cases (earlier spread over two to five positions), A20 reaches A32 five positions later in about 99 in 100 (earlier spread), and reverse pairs such as A24 before A20 or A26 before A22 were observed only once or twice in the later window. [LAG031, LAG010, LAG014, LAG036, LAG019, LAG027]
- A08 became far less common: it appeared in about 72 in 100 traces earlier versus about 29 in 100 later. Its co-occurrence with A14, A15, A16, A20–A26, A31, A32, A47 and A48 fell accordingly (together in 72 of 100 traces earlier, 29 of 100 later; partner alone rose from 28 to 71). After A15, the flow now continues to A16 in about 87 in 100 of that activity's outgoing transitions (was 58) and to A08 in about 7 (was 42); A08's own exits spread from 90 in 100 to A16 towards A16 (39), A48 (16) and A15 (15). [OCC001, REL001, REL003, REL010, DIR003, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002]
- A10 became more common: about 8 in 100 traces earlier versus about 22 in 100 later; its outgoing transitions shifted towards A48 (about 31 in 100) and A16 (14), while A30 (earlier 21) and A31 (14) left its profile. [OCC002, DIR004]
- Smaller redistributions: A14→A15 fell from about 98 to 82 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions, and A47→A48 from about 98 to 80, with small new exits from A47 to A08 and A10; the successor profiles of A02 and A04 also changed strongly but rest on only about 15–40 outgoing transitions per window, so they are weakly grounded. [DIR005, DIR015, LAG037, DIR001, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the ordering constraints among A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 changed: a group of activities that earlier ran in several, partly unfixed orders between A31 and A32 is now executed as one fixed sequence, A31 → A22 → A20 → A23 → A24 → A26 → A25 → A32. This rests on direct relational and positional evidence rather than volume: all six activities occur together in every trace in both windows, so participation did not change; each activity's outgoing transitions collapsed to a single dominant successor (about 90–99 in 100, versus split and back-and-forth exits earlier); every tested pair inside the group switched to one order; and inter-activity distances now match the chain position by position while the reverse directions nearly disappeared. With 76 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed (187 units tested), chance re-sampling cannot explain the differences as a whole. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, DIR013, REL014, REL016, REL017, REL019, REL021, LAG006, LAG010, LAG011, LAG031, LAG036]

An important competing explanation remains: the earlier window may simply have mixed several pre-existing execution variants of which the later window retains essentially one — a shift in the frequency of existing paths rather than a new sequencing rule — and the aggregate indicators cannot separate these two. A few reverse-order conclusions also rest on single observations in the later window. [LAG019, LAG025, LAG027]

Other differences: A08's participation fell from about 72 to 29 in 100 traces, with A15 now usually continuing to A16 instead of A08 and A08's own exits spreading from A16 to A48 and A15; A10's participation rose from about 8 to 22 in 100 traces, with exits shifting towards A48 and A16. The evidence does not show how these participation changes relate to the reordering above. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR006, REL001, LAG001]
